correctness.rationale: The displayed cubic is smooth for p>5. Its geometric lines split into 15 rational diagonal lines and six quadratic-conjugate skew pairs; in nonsplit Frobenius fields, conjugate lines meet no rational points. The 15 diagonal lines form the (15,6,1,3) incidence graph, with ten Eckardt triple points and fifteen double points. All 27 lines are rational when the character of 5 is positive; 135 meeting line pairs minus 30 pair incidences at Eckardt points leave 105 ordinary double points. The Picard intersection matrix of the diagonals has rank six and Frobenius trace five in nonsplit, trace seven in split, giving #X(Q)=Q^2+5Q+1 or Q^2+7Q+1. Subtracting line unions gives N0=Q^2-10Q+21 or Q^2-20Q+99; extension alternation generates the zeta factors. Tangent quadratic forms exclude extra Eckardt triples for p>5. Independent prime-field point counting gave Q7=0,Q11=0,Q13=60 and matches derived formulas, not an all-field proof.
